sections.heading: Principles & evolution of India's foreign policy

blocks.text: India's foreign policy, rooted in **Nehru's Panchsheel and Non-Alignment**, has evolved from **Cold-War non-alignment to post-1991 pragmatic multi-alignment** — pursuing **strategic autonomy, economic diplomacy and multipolarity** while championing the Global South.

rows: **Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence** (India-China agreement) — mutual respect, non-aggression, non-interference, equality, coexistence.
Founded **1961 (Belgrade)** — Nehru, Nasser, Tito; independence from both Cold-War blocs.
**Economic diplomacy, Look East → Act East, strategic autonomy, multi-alignment**.
**Gujral Doctrine, Neighbourhood First, Act East, SAGAR (maritime), Indo-Pacific, Vaccine Maitri**.
**Strategic autonomy, national interest, multipolar world, Global South leadership**.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: India's foreign policy

items: **Foundations**: **Panchsheel (1954)** — 5 principles of peaceful coexistence; **Non-Aligned Movement (NAM, 1961 Belgrade — Nehru, Nasser, Tito)**; anti-colonialism; strategic autonomy.

**Evolution**: 1962 (China war) & 1971 (Bangladesh + Indo-Soviet Treaty) shifts to realism; **1974/1998 nuclear tests**; post-1991 **Look East → Act East**; **Neighbourhood First, SAGAR (maritime), Indo-Pacific, Vaccine Maitri**.
**Doctrines/partnerships**: strategic partnership with the US (Quad), Russia, EU, Japan; **Gujral Doctrine** (non-reciprocity with neighbours).
**Determinants**: geography, history, economy, security (China-Pakistan), diaspora, energy; parliamentary oversight; MEA.
Panchsheel (1954, 5 principles); NAM (1961 Belgrade); post-1991 = pragmatic multi-alignment.
Key policies: Neighbourhood First, Act East, SAGAR, strategic autonomy.
